extracted.intended_audience: bacterial taxonomists, systematists, microbiologists, and nomenclature practitioners preparing or evaluating prokaryote names
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of Judicial Commission Opinions interpreting and applying the International Code of Nomenclature of Bacteria: rules for conserving or rejecting names, typification (type/neotype strains), corrections to Approved Lists, and other formal nomenclatural actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation of a specific epithet against earlier synonyms
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific epithet “phenylpyruvica” in the name Moraxella phenylpyruvica Bøvre and Henriksen 1967 is conserved against the specific epithet “polymorpha” in the name of the earlier objective synonym Moraxella polymorpha Flamm 1957 and against the specific epithets in all other earlier objective synonyms. The neotype strain of Moraxella phenylpyruvica is 2863 (= ATCC 23333 = NCTC 10526).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conservation preserves a later-used epithet over earlier objective synonyms to maintain stability; conservation may be accompanied by designation of a neotype strain. Examples in the text include phenylpyruvica, sphaeroides, avium, fermentum, fortuitum.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation of specific epithet for organisms with earlier subjective synonyms
rubrics_metrics.description: The specific epithet “sphaeroides” in the name Rhodopseudomonas sphaeroides van Niel 1944 is conserved against the specific epithet “minor” in the name of the earlier subjective synonym Rhodococcus minor and against the specific epithets in the names of all earlier objective synonyms of Rhodopseudomonas sphaeroides. The neotype strain is van Niel’s ATH 2.4.1 (= ATCC 17023).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conservation can be invoked to preserve long-established usage even when earlier subjective synonyms exist; neotype designation may accompany conservation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation of generic names and type species (generic conservation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The generic name Rhodopseudomonas Czurda and Maresch 1937 emend. van Niel 1944 is conserved over all earlier objective synonyms; the type species is Rhodopseudomonas palustris (Molisch 1907) van Niel 1944 (basonym Rhodobacillus palustris Molisch 1907).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Generic conservation secures a genus name and an associated type species over earlier synonyms to stabilise nomenclature; may include emendations and explicit type species designation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Placement of names on the List of Rejected Names (nomina rejicienda) for being nomen dubium/ambiguum/perplexum/confusum
rubrics_metrics.description: The name Leuconostoc citrovorum (Hammer 1920) Hucker and Pederson 1931, together with its objective synonyms, is regarded as a nomen dubium and is placed on the list of rejected names. Similarly, Aerobacter Beijerinck 1900 is regarded as a nomen ambiguum and is placed on the list of rejected generic names.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Names that cause confusion, are applied incorrectly, are ambiguous, or lack clear application can be rejected and placed on the nomina rejicienda list. Examples: Leuconostoc citrovorum, Aerobacter liquefaciens, Mycobacterium marianum, Pseudomonas denitrificans, Mycobacterium aquae, Peptococcus anaerobius, Pelczaria aurantia.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation or replacement of type strains / neotype strains
rubrics_metrics.description: The type strain of Acetobacter aceti subsp. xylinum is NCIB 11664 (≡ NCIB 4112B) not ATCC 23767. The neotype strain of Moraxella phenylpyruvica is 2863 (= ATCC 23333 = NCTC 10526). Strain ATCC 27377 is rejected as the type strain of Pasteuria ramosa and the species is conserved with the description of Metchnikoff, as amended, serving as the type.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an originally designated type strain is incorrect, unrepresentative, lost, or inconsistent with the original description, the Commission may reject that strain and designate/confirm a replacement type or neotype. Rationale examples include misidentification, non-authentic cultures, or inconsistency with original descriptive material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conservation and emendation when type species are transferred
rubrics_metrics.description: Methanococcus mazei, the type species of Methanococcus, is transferred to Methanosarcina as Methanosarcina mazei (Barker 1936) comb. nov. et emend. Mah and Kuhn 1984. The genus Methanococcus (Approved Lists 1980) emend. Mah and Kuhn 1984 is conserved with Methanococcus vannielii as the type species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When taxa are reclassified, the Commission can conserve genus names with amended type species to preserve nomenclatural stability despite transfers of taxa between genera.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection or correction of names that contravene specific Rules of the Code
rubrics_metrics.description: The genus Methanothrix with the species Methanothrix soehngenii was placed on the list of nomina rejicienda because it is not represented by an axenic culture and contravenes Rule 31a of the International Code of Nomenclature of Bacteria. Also, publication and typification issues relating to Rules 27(3) and 30 are addressed in Opinions (e.g., lists of names not in accordance with these rules).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-compliance with explicit Code rules (e.g., concerning axenic cultures, deposition in culture collections, valid publication requirements) is a ground for rejection, correction, or conditional validation. The Opinions cite Rules 12b, 27(3), 30, 31a, 40d, 51b, 53, 54, etc., as operative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejection of names that could have serious consequences for human welfare and health
rubrics_metrics.description: The name Yersinia pseudotuberculosis subsp. pestis (van Loghem) Bercovier et al. 1981 is placed on the list of nomina rejicienda because the use of the name could have serious consequences for human welfare and health. The name Yersinia pestis is conserved for the plague bacillus.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public-health implications or potential for confusion with dangerous pathogens can justify rejection of a name even where taxonomic relatedness exists; welfare/health risks are explicit grounds for action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typification must be based on authentic type material; lack of axenic culture invalidates names
rubrics_metrics.description: The genus Methanothrix with the species Methanothrix soehngenii was placed on the list of nomina rejicienda, based on the fact that it is not represented by an axenic culture and contravenes Rule 31a of the Code.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a name lacks authentic type material (e.g., no axenic culture) as required, it may be rejected or require replacement typification; the Commission enforces typification requirements strictly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction of gender or grammatical form of specific epithets
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judicial Commission adjusted the gender of the specific epithet to durus (masculine) and decided that the name Paenibacillus durus has priority over Paenibacillus azotofixans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Epithet endings may be corrected to agree in gender with the generic name, and such corrections are formal actions that affect priority and valid name usage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship and citation corrections for combinations and names
rubrics_metrics.description: The combination Enterobacter agglomerans is to be cited as Enterobacter agglomerans (Beijerinck 1888) Ewing and Fife 1972 and the combination Pantoea agglomerans is to be cited as Pantoea agglomerans (Beijerinck 1888) Gavini et al. 1989.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission specifies authoritative forms for citing authorship of names and combinations; proper citation affects clarity and historical attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duplication of identical epithets based on different types creates illegitimate epithets requiring replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: The epithet aurantiaca in Micromonospora aurantiaca Sveshnikova et al. 1969 (Approved Lists 1980) is illegitimate because the specific epithet aurantiaca is the same as the subspecific epithet aurantiaca in Micromonospora carbonacea subsp. aurantiaca Luedemann and Brodsky 1964 (Approved Lists 1980). According to Rule 53 the duplication creates an illegitimate epithet with priority determining which is to be replaced as specified in Rule 54.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When identical epithets are based on different types within a genus, the later one is illegitimate and must be replaced following the Code's priority and replacement rules; authorship of the original must be retained when replacing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valid publication depends on documented deposition in culture collections (Rules 27(3) and 30)
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on a list of names proposed in original articles or cited in Validation Lists from January 2001 that are not in accordance with Rules 27(3) and 30, the Judicial Commission rules names in certain lists to be considered validly published only if deposit in more than one collection in different countries is documented.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Valid publication of a name requires proper, documented deposition of type strains in culture collections (often in multiple countries) as specified by the Code; absence of such documentation affects validity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confirmed typification in the Approved Lists supersedes earlier usages but remains amendable by the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: The names of the bacterial taxa cited in the Approved Lists of Bacterial Names are formally and explicitly confirmed as correct and supersede any others in use before the appearance of the lists but without prejudice to the powers of the Judicial Commission to amend them.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approved Lists confer formal standing to names and typifications, providing stability, but the Commission retains authority to amend typifications when necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Corrections to the Approved Lists of Bacterial Names according to Rule 40d (authorship corrections)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judicial Commission affirms that, according to Rule 40d, formerly Rule 46, of the Bacteriological Code, the authorship of a number of subspecies names included on the Approved Lists of Bacterial Names must be corrected (examples listed in the Opinion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission issues formal author-citation corrections for entries on the Approved Lists to ensure bibliographic and nomenclatural accuracy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Names above the rank of class should be discouraged and names at class/subclass/order with unclear typification placed on rejected lists
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judicial Commission ruled that names at the rank of class and order proposed by Cavalier-Smith are to be placed on the List of Rejected Names and the use of names proposed above the rank of class is to be actively discouraged. A list is given where the nomenclatural type, description or circumscription is unclear or not in accordance with the Rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission discourages publication of names above class rank and will reject names where typification or circumscription is unclear or non-compliant with the Code.

rubrics_metrics.name: Commission may decline to adjudicate taxonomic assignments that are outside nomenclatural scope
rubrics_metrics.description: In issuing this opinion the Judicial Commission declines to comment on the assignment of strain ATCC 27377 to another genus because this is a taxonomic matter and not one of nomenclature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission confines itself to nomenclatural questions (names, typification, validity) and will not rule on taxonomic or phylogenetic classifications except insofar as they affect nomenclature.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strains derived from original isolates may serve as type strains even if not designated neotypes
rubrics_metrics.description: Strain NCIMB 13488 will not be the neotype, but since it is derived from strain NRC 34021, which in turn is derived from Petter’s original isolate, it is 'a strain on which the original description was based' [Rule 18c] and may therefore also serve as the type strain of the species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A strain descended from the original material and linked to the original description can be accepted as the type strain under Code rules even if not formally designated as a neotype, provided the lineage is demonstrable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replacement of type strains used historically when they are shown not to represent authentic cultures
rubrics_metrics.description: The Judicial Commission decided that strain NCTC 4175, used as the neotype strain of Proteus vulgaris since 1963, be replaced by strain ATCC 29905. Similarly, ATCC 43642 replaces ATCC 23581 as the type strain of Leptospira interrogans because the latter does not represent an authentic culture of the original strain.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When historical type/neotype strains are demonstrated not to represent the authentic original material, the Commission may replace them with authenticated strains to restore correct typification.
